lessons.title: Firinscneach uatha: an + séimhiú
lessons.en: Masculine nouns: keep an and lenite
lessons.rule: After a compound preposition (i gcoinne, i ndiaidh, ar chúl) the noun goes into the genitive: for a masculine noun keep an and lenite b, c, f, g, m or p (an cat: i ndiaidh an chait), then give it its genitive ending.
steps: i gcoinne is a compound preposition, so the noun goes into the genitive.
geata is masculine: keep an and lenite g: an gheata.
geata keeps the same ending: Tá an rothar ina sheasamh i gcoinne an gheata.

example.prompt: Tá an rothar ina sheasamh i gcoinne (an geata).
example.answer: Tá an rothar ina sheasamh i gcoinne an gheata.

lessons.title: Firinscneach uatha: d, t, l, n, r, s agus gutaí
lessons.en: Masculine nouns beginning with d, t, l, n, r, s or a vowel
lessons.rule: A masculine noun beginning with d, t, l, n or r takes no séimhiú after an (i gcoinne an rialtais); s before a vowel or l, n, r takes t (an tseó), and a vowel loses its t- (an tAifreann: an Aifrinn). Then give the noun its genitive ending.
steps: in aice takes the genitive, and droichead is masculine, so keep an.
droichead begins with d, so do not lenite it.
Change the ending to the genitive, droichid: Chuaigh muid ag snámh in aice an droichid.

example.prompt: Chuaigh muid ag snámh in aice (an droichead).
example.answer: Chuaigh muid ag snámh in aice an droichid.

more.answer: Tá bruscar caite ar fud an tsráidbhaile.

lessons.hint: No séimhiú on d, t, l, n, r; s takes t; drop the t- before a vowel.

lessons.title: Baininscneach uatha: na, gan séimhiú
lessons.en: Feminine nouns: an becomes na, lenition goes
lessons.rule: For a feminine noun, change an to na and take away the séimhiú or the t that an gave it (an fhoireann: na foirne; an tseachtain: na seachtaine), then give it its genitive ending.
steps: sráid is feminine, so an becomes na.
Take away the t that an gave it: na sráid.
Add the genitive ending -e: Tá an bus ina stad i lár na sráide.

example.prompt: Tá an bus ina stad i lár (an tsráid).
example.answer: Tá an bus ina stad i lár na sráide.

more.answer: Tá crann os comhair na fuinneoige.

lessons.hint: Feminine: na, no séimhiú, no t.

lessons.title: Baininscneach uatha: consan gan athrú, h roimh ghuta
lessons.en: Feminine nouns: no change to a consonant, h before a vowel
lessons.rule: When a feminine noun has no séimhiú to take away, na leaves a consonant alone (na scoile) and puts h before a vowel (an oifig: na hoifige). Then give it its genitive ending.
steps: os comhair takes the genitive, and oifig is feminine, so an becomes na.
oifig begins with a vowel, so put h before it: na hoifig.
Add the genitive ending -e: Tá Aoife ina seasamh os comhair na hoifige.

example.prompt: Tá Aoife ina seasamh os comhair (an oifig).
example.answer: Tá Aoife ina seasamh os comhair na hoifige.

more.answer: Bhí muid ag siúl in aice na trá.

lessons.hint: na + consonant: no change; na + vowel: add h.

lessons.title: An t-iolra: na + urú
lessons.rule: In the plural, use na and eclipse the noun (na daltaí: na ndaltaí; na hamhránaithe: na n-amhránaithe). A plural like gasúir that ends in a slender consonant goes back to the singular shape: na ngasúr.
steps: os cionn takes the genitive, and tithe is plural, so use na.
Eclipse t to dt: na dtithe.
tithe keeps its ending: Tá an drón os cionn na dtithe.

example.prompt: Tá an drón os cionn (na tithe).
example.answer: Tá an drón os cionn na dtithe.

lessons.title: Ainmfhocal gan alt
lessons.rule: With no article, add nothing in front and do not lenite: just give the noun its genitive form (ar lorg airgid, ar feadh bliana, i gceann míosa). After mo, do or a, keep the change they make: i gcoinne mo thola.
steps: ar feadh takes the genitive, and there is no article, so add nothing in front.
Change coicís to its genitive form: coicíse.
Bhí sí ar saoire ar feadh coicíse.

example.answer: Bhí sí ar saoire ar feadh coicíse.
